entries.t: Two days after the Gachibowli building collapse killed two workers, Cyberabad flags 38 illegal buildings and demolishes nine
entries.s: Two days after an illegal seven-storey building under construction on a 50-square-yard Anjaiah Nagar (Gachibowli) plot collapsed and killed two migrant workers, Cyberabad Municipal Corporation Commissioner G. Srijana ordered a city-wide sweep for unauthorised under-construction buildings. Teams flagged 38 such buildings, served notices on 28, seized one, and demolished nine — while HYDRAA resumed demolishing a second structurally damaged building at the original site using its high-reach "Bahubali" machine. Why it matters to you: the enforcement rule used here is exactly the one that governs small plots — under 75 sq. yards, anything over 7 metres (roughly ground+1) needs full sanction, and this crackdown shows officials are actively hunting for exactly that violation right now across Cyberabad, not just at the collapse site.
entries.src: Sources: Telangana Today, Deccan Chronicle, NewsMeter & The Hans India · published 24 Aug 2026 (Monday; exact clock time not stated in source)

entries.t: Assembly session confirmed for 7 September — CM tells MLAs to speed up land acquisition, with the CURE and Land Pooling Bills expected on the floor
entries.s: CM A. Revanth Reddy told MLAs at a Secretariat meeting that the Legislative Assembly's monsoon session will begin on 7 September, and directed them to expedite pending land acquisition for irrigation projects, promising funds for acquisition, Relief & Rehabilitation and forest clearances. The statewide Land Pooling Bill (landowners reportedly getting back 60% of developed plots, HMDA/TGIIC keeping 40%) and the CURE Bill replacing the GHMC Act are both expected to come up in that session. Why it matters to you: 7 September is now the date to actually watch for the land-pooling framework's fine print — ratios, eligibility, who administers it — rather than the vaguer "coming soon" you've heard so far.
entries.src: Sources: IANS, Siasat, Deccan Chronicle & The Hans India · published 24 Aug 2026, 11:13 PM IST (IANS wire)

entries.t: Back in Hyderabad, Revanth Reddy calls the US-trip denial "an insult to Telangana," accuses the Centre of political bias — but ducks the Konda Surekha question
entries.s: At a press conference at the Secretariat, CM A. Revanth Reddy said the Ministry of External Affairs's denial of political clearance for the US leg of his tour was "not a denial to Revanth Reddy but a disrespect to the people of Telangana," asking why the UK leg was cleared but not the US one if nothing political was involved. He called it "Gujarat supremacy" and demanded PM Modi explain personally, while confirming the Telangana Global Summit 2026 for 8–9 December. Asked about Konda Surekha, he declined comment, saying the party disciplinary process must run its course. Why it matters to you: the CM is now fully engaged domestically — watch whether that translates into actual movement on the Konda Surekha Cabinet question and the pending land bills, rather than another round of Centre-state sparring.
entries.src: Sources: ANI (17:53 IST), The Tribune, Siasat, Deccan Chronicle & Prokerala · published 24 Aug 2026

entries.t: Government hits back on Section 22A: Revenue Minister says 98% of registrations already cleared, forms a 15-day fast-track committee for Hyderabad's four districts
entries.s: Answering BRS's Harish Rao, Revenue Minister Ponguleti Srinivas Reddy said claims that "lakhs of acres" were wrongly frozen under Section 22A were a "misleading Opposition campaign," and that 98% of registrations sought under the provision have already been cleared. Of 980 distinct grievance-line complaints (547 agricultural, 433 non-agricultural) and over 300 relaxation requests, only 12–13 were rejected. He announced a high-level committee — the Revenue Principal Secretary, the IG of Registration and Stamps, and district officials from Hyderabad, Rangareddy, Sangareddy and Medchal-Malkajgiri — to review genuine cases daily for 15 days, with fees refunded within a week and grievances resolved in 24–36 hours. Why it matters to you: this is the most actionable 22A news since the crisis began — a named 15-day window (ending roughly 8 September) and a specific toll-free/committee process across the four districts that cover almost all of metro Hyderabad's plotting activity. If you have a frozen survey number, this is the process to actually use.
entries.src: Sources: Siasat, NTV Telugu, NewsMeter & Telangana Tribune · published 24 Aug 2026 (Monday, Secretariat press conference)

entries.t: Report: Congress high command gives Konda Surekha a resign-by-this-evening ultimatum; minister refuses
entries.s: The Hans India reports the Congress high command asked Endowments & Forest Minister Konda Surekha, via a senior minister from erstwhile Nalgonda district, to resign by Tuesday (today) evening or face dismissal — and that she has refused, maintaining she made no remarks against the CM or party. This follows her 23 August meeting with AICC chief Kharge, who reportedly told her to settle the matter with the TPCC rather than the high command. Why it matters to you: unconfirmed by a second outlet, so treat as a rumour with a deadline rather than fact — but if her Endowments & Forest portfolio does change hands today, note who replaces her, since that person will administer land bordering exactly the categories you need to watch.
entries.src: Source: The Hans India · published 24–25 Aug 2026 (single-sourced — no independent confirmation found; flagged as developing)

entries.t: Karnataka Legislature passes ₹7,042.69-crore supplementary budget with ₹1,000 crore earmarked for Bengaluru road infrastructure, then adjourns sine die three days early
entries.s: Amid the Opposition's protest over Minister B. Nagendra (see Karnataka Politics), the Karnataka Legislature passed a first-instalment supplementary budget of ₹7,042.69 crore (₹4,324.35 crore revenue, ₹2,718.35 crore capital) before Speaker G.S. Patil adjourned the Monsoon Session sine die — three days ahead of its scheduled 27 August finish. The capital allocation includes ₹1,000 crore earmarked for Bengaluru road development. The Government Parks (Preservation) Amendment Bill, Cabinet-cleared on 21–22 August to allow up to 5% of any park to be alienated for infrastructure, was reported by some outlets as passed the same day — we could not independently confirm Assembly passage of that specific bill , so treat its status as still "Cabinet-cleared, not yet law" until confirmed. Why it matters to you: ₹1,000 crore for Bengaluru roads is a real, funded infrastructure line — worth tracking which corridors it targets, since road spending is one of the more reliable early signals of where land values move next. The park-land bill is not yet law, whatever some reports implied — don't act on it as settled.
entries.src: Sources: countryandpolitics.in, The Hans India & ANI · published 24 Aug 2026

entries.t: The siege happened: police detain Vijayendra, Ashoka and CT Ravi at Vidhana Soudha; Assembly then adjourned sine die, three days early, with Nagendra still in his job
entries.s: The BJP-JD(S) march from Freedom Park to Vidhana Soudha went ahead at 9:30 AM on 24 August as announced. Police blocked all gates and pre-emptively detained BJP state president B.Y. Vijayendra, Leader of the Opposition R. Ashoka and senior leader CT Ravi, along with many cadre. Ashoka accused police of rough handling and announced an indefinite day-and-night Assembly dharna until Minister B. Nagendra resigns over the Valmiki Corporation scam — but the Speaker adjourned the session sine die that same day, three days ahead of schedule, effectively ending the sitting the Opposition had vowed to occupy. BJP leaders then marched to Raj Bhavan and petitioned Governor Thawarchand Gehlot to seek an explanation from CM D.K. Shivakumar. Nagendra has not resigned. Why it matters to you: same lesson as yesterday, now with a harder edge — the government let the whole Assembly session end early rather than remove one minister. When an institution will sacrifice its own legislative calendar to protect a person, that person (or whoever controls what he controls) is more important to the power structure than the session itself.
entries.src: Sources: ANI (multiple wires, 10:08 AM–2:50 PM IST), Deccan Herald, The Statesman, The Week & Deccan Chronicle · published 24 Aug 2026

entries.t: Karnataka's first SIR draft electoral roll cuts 1.07 crore names — nearly half of Bengaluru's voter list flagged for review
entries.s: Karnataka's Special Intensive Revision (SIR) draft electoral roll shows 4.47 crore voters, down from 5.54 crore — 1.07 crore names (about 19%) moved to an "Absent/Shifted/Dead/Duplicate/Other" category pending verification. In Bengaluru alone, 46.88 lakh of 1.03 crore voters (45%) are flagged, split almost evenly between BJP-held and Congress-held seats. Claims and objections run 24 August–23 September; the final roll is due 27 October. Why it matters to you: not a land story directly, but a reminder of how fast a "provisional" government list — voter roll today, survey number tomorrow — can knock someone off a register pending paperwork. The same discipline (check, don't assume) applies to both.
entries.src: Sources: Siasat, Deccan Herald & Scroll.in · published 24 Aug 2026

entries.t: 🎓 Buying farm land near a city: an investment guide
entries.s: Peri-urban farmland is really a bet on the city's growth, not on crops. Priced that way, it can be excellent — sold as farm income, it is usually a trap.
entries.src: Land School · class 1 of today’s 2 · topic: Buying · source & further reading: 1acre.in

entries.t: 🎓 Capital gains tax on agricultural land sale
entries.s: Rural farmland is not a capital asset at all — zero capital gains tax. The test is mechanical: census population and aerial kilometres. Urban farmland is taxed, with 54B and 54EC as the exits.
entries.src: Land School · class 2 of today’s 2 · topic: Tax · source & further reading: 1acre.in

entries.t: Revanth Reddy flies home from London after the Centre blocks his US leg on a "political" ground — and promises to "speak in Hyderabad"
entries.s: Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy cut short his "Telangana Rising" tour and returned to Hyderabad from London on 23 August, after the Ministry of External Affairs cleared the UK leg but denied political clearance for the US leg, which the MEA said involved a "planned programme not appropriate to the office held." Revanth called the denial politically motivated and said he would explain the matter in detail at a press conference once back in Hyderabad. He thanked AICC president Mallikarjun Kharge for his backing and, rather than cancel outright, ordered the official delegation to continue to the US to sign MoUs with Harvard, MIT, Northeastern and Virginia Tech in his absence. Why it matters to you: the CM is now physically back in Hyderabad — the trigger multiple reports said could unlock decisions on the Konda Surekha Cabinet question and other pending matters. Watch what he actually does in the next few days, not what the tour headlines promised: the investment MoUs are intent, not funded projects.
entries.src: Sources: ANI, The South First, Deccan Herald & The Hans India · published 23 Aug 2026 (ANI wire timestamped ~8:17 PM IST)

entries.t: Harish Rao threatens to stall the Assembly and gherao the Secretariat over Section 22A — names three colonies he wants struck off the freeze list
entries.s: BRS deputy floor leader T. Harish Rao escalated the Section 22A land-freeze fight at a party meeting in Boduppal supporting affected residents, warning that BRS would stall the coming Assembly session and lay siege to ("gherao") the Secretariat if the Congress government does not withdraw what he called unjust prohibitory listings. He specifically demanded that Tirumala Meadows, Lakshmi Ganapathi and Hemanagar colonies be removed from the Section 22A restricted list, alleging fully registered houses were being placed under the freeze to enable illegal collections, and that middle-class families could no longer get bank loans or sell their properties as a result. Why it matters to you: this is the exact mechanism that can freeze a plot mid-deal — a registered, patta property swept onto the 22A list. Note the named colonies (all Boduppal/Medchal-Malkajgiri side) as elevated-risk zones, and treat "it's registered" as necessary but not sufficient until you've personally checked the live 22A list for the survey number.
entries.src: Sources: Deccan Chronicle, Telangana Today & The Hans India · published 23 Aug 2026 (exact clock time not stated in source)

entries.t: Konda Surekha flies to Bengaluru to meet Kharge — who tells her to settle the rift with the state unit, not the high command
entries.s: Endowments & Forest Minister Konda Surekha met AICC president Mallikarjun Kharge in Bengaluru (reportedly for about 15 minutes) to brief him on the Congress rift caused by her daughter Konda Sushmita's remarks against CM Revanth Reddy. Surekha maintained that neither she nor her daughter had criticised the party or the Gandhi family and alleged a conspiracy targeting her family. Kharge reportedly expressed displeasure, cautioned her against remarks that hurt party interests, and told her to resolve it with the TPCC. No formal Cabinet decision on her position has been reported. Why it matters to you: her portfolio covers Endowments & Forest land — two of the trickiest boundary categories a plotting developer can run into. A reshuffle here is worth tracking, but the takeaway today is the political grammar: going over the state unit's head to the high command got her sent right back down to the state unit.
entries.src: Sources: The Hans India & NTV Telugu · published 23 Aug 2026 (Sunday; exact clock time not stated in source)

entries.t: KTR sets a week-long BRS offensive from Sept 2, timed to the Congress government's 1,000th day: "not one promise fully kept"
entries.s: BRS Working President K.T. Rama Rao (KTR) announced a statewide week-long campaign starting 2 September, timed to the Congress government completing 1,000 days in office, to spotlight what BRS calls its "betrayal" of election promises. KTR said Congress made 420 promises, 13 declarations and six guarantees claiming implementation within 100 days, but had "not fully fulfilled even a single promise" after 1,000 days. He directed cadres to hand out "Baaki Cards" (pending-dues cards) listing unfulfilled welfare commitments to each social group. Why it matters to you: a milestone-timed opposition campaign is a signal, not noise — it tells you which promises the government will feel most pressure to be seen delivering. Anything land- or housing-linked (2BHK schemes, plot regularisation, compensation) tends to get pushed hardest in exactly these anniversary windows.
entries.src: Sources: ANI & Siasat · published 24 Aug 2026 (ANI wire timestamped ~2:44 AM IST)

entries.t: BJP and JD(S) announce a siege of Vidhana Soudha this morning over the Valmiki Corporation scam — demanding Minister Nagendra's removal
entries.s: Karnataka Leader of the Opposition R. Ashoka announced that the BJP, with ally JD(S), would march from Freedom Park and lay siege to Vidhana Soudha at 9:30 AM on Monday, 24 August, demanding the removal of Planning & Statistics Minister B. Nagendra over the Karnataka Maharshi Valmiki Scheduled Tribes Development Corporation scam. Ashoka said an initial ₹89 crore was illegally transferred from the corporation's Union Bank account to various accounts, with the overall alleged diversion later pegged at about ₹187 crore — money he claimed was used to fund Congress campaigns. He said JD(S) chief H.D. Kumaraswamy backed continuing the agitation for another week, and that the BJP had compiled details of 35 cases against Nagendra spanning mining and the Valmiki Corporation. Why it matters to you: this is the same pattern as yesterday's story — the government gave Nagendra an extra portfolio rather than remove him. The lesson for a developer is institutional: watch what happens to a minister who controls large discretionary funds under fire — a government that digs in is telling you where real power sits, which is what actually governs how discretionary land and money get allotted.
entries.src: Sources: ANI, Siasat, Deccan Chronicle & The Hans India · published 23 Aug 2026 (ANI wire timestamped ~12:43 PM IST); the siege itself is scheduled for 9:30 AM 24 Aug — after press time

entries.t: BJP chief Vijayendra vows to fight Karnataka's park-land bill: a "systematic conspiracy" to take over protected green space
entries.s: Karnataka BJP president B.Y. Vijayendra said the party would "make every possible effort to prevent" the Karnataka Government Parks (Preservation) Amendment Bill, calling it "a systematic conspiracy to take over government parks reserved for environmental protection, public health safeguards and other public uses." The bill, cleared by Cabinet on 21–22 August, would let up to 5% of any government park or garden be alienated — sold, leased, gifted, exchanged or mortgaged — for public infrastructure. Critics tie it to the roughly ₹17,770-crore Hebbal–Silk Board tunnel road, which reportedly needs about six acres of Lalbagh temporarily and one acre permanently. Why it matters to you: yesterday you learned the bill exists; today's lesson is that "Cabinet cleared" is only step one — it still needs Assembly passage, Council, and the Governor's assent, and an organised opposition can slow or reshape it at each stage. Never treat a protected-land carve-out as done until it's notified.
entries.src: Sources: The Federal & ANI wire (syndicated) · published 23 Aug 2026 (exact clock time not stated in source)

entries.t: TPCC panel finds Konda Surekha's daughter "crossed the limits" — but defers action; minister counter-complains against her own party's rebel MLAs
entries.s: Telangana's TPCC Disciplinary Committee, chaired by Lok Sabha MP Mallu Ravi, met for over three hours at Gandhi Bhavan to review showcause replies from Minister Konda Surekha and senior leader G. Chinna Reddy. It informally concluded that Surekha's daughter Konda Sushmita had "crossed the limits" attacking CM Revanth Reddy, and that Surekha herself was at fault for not condemning the remarks — but deferred any formal decision, saying it will meet again. Surekha separately wrote to Mallu Ravi asking the committee to instead investigate the 20+ Congress MLAs demanding her sacking, and whether outside forces are trying to influence its judgment. Why it matters to you: CM Revanth Reddy returns to Hyderabad from London around today, and reports suggest he may take "crucial decisions" on Surekha's Cabinet position soon after — any reshuffle of the Endowments & Forest portfolio is worth tracking if you deal near forest or endowment land boundaries.
entries.src: Sources: Deccan Chronicle, Telangana Today, The Hans India & Great Andhra · published 22 Aug 2026 (exact clock time not stated in source)

entries.t: Revanth pitches Cambridge and London for a Hyderabad "knowledge hub" — but an Oxford meeting ignites a fresh BJP "anti-national" row, and BRS alleges a hawala-linked MoU tied to the CM's brother
entries.s: Telangana's "Telangana Rising" delegation, still in London, met academic teams from Cambridge and the University of London on Saturday to pitch Hyderabad as a future "global knowledge hub"; Cambridge Judge Business School professors Jaideep Prabhu and Venkata Serish Gandikota reportedly expressed interest, and University of London officials discussed a possible Hyderabad campus. But an earlier Oxford meeting with professors Maya Tudor and Faisal Devji — both known for writing critical of Indian democracy and nationalism — became a political flashpoint, with BJP leaders publicly slamming Revanth for meeting figures they call "anti-India." Separately, BRS's Manne Krishank called the Centre's US-leg denial a "diplomatic embarrassment" and asked "is this some sort of hawala business?", alleging an earlier ₹1,000-crore MoU the CM signed in the US involved "Swachh Bio," a new firm owned by his brother Anumula Jagadishwar Reddy. Why it matters to you: a reminder that a state's glossy MoU-tour announcements are marketing, not commitments — MoUs with Harvard, MIT and Cambridge are still just intent until they clear every layer of scrutiny and actually get funded and built.
entries.src: Sources: ANI, Deccan Chronicle, Organiser & Asianet Newsable · published 22 Aug 2026 (BJP reaction reported ~2:51 PM IST per ANI)

entries.t: GO 97 protests, round two: Technical Education Commissioner holds fresh talks with polytechnic students — they leave unsatisfied
entries.s: Commissioner of Technical Education A. Sridevasena held talks with polytechnic student representatives over GO 97's plan to fold polytechnics into the new Young India Skill University. Students left the meeting dissatisfied, still demanding the order be withdrawn entirely over fears of fee hikes and a devalued diploma. Why it matters to you: a second round of talks without resolution usually means the underlying order stands — worth remembering that a Government Order, once issued, is genuinely hard to reverse even under sustained protest.
entries.src: Sources: Telangana Today & Namasthe Telangana (Telugu, BRS-aligned outlet) · published 22 Aug 2026 (exact clock time not stated in source)

entries.t: Karnataka Cabinet clears a bill to let government carve up to 5% of any park or garden — Cubbon Park and Lalbagh included — for infrastructure projects
entries.s: The Karnataka Cabinet approved a Bill amending the Karnataka Government Parks (Preservation) Act, 1975, to allow up to 5% of any government park or garden's total area to be "alienated" — sold, leased, gifted, exchanged or mortgaged — for public infrastructure or utility projects, restricted to government departments, statutory authorities and local bodies. A high-level committee headed by an Additional Chief Secretary-rank officer will vet which land qualifies. BJP state president B.Y. Vijayendra called it "detrimental to the environment," and MP Tejasvi Surya said "parks are not real-estate assets," alleging the bill exists to route around a pending court challenge to the Hebbal–Silk Board tunnel road project (bid leader: Adani Group) on Parks Act grounds. Why it matters to you: watch this as a precedent — a government rewriting a protective land-use law specifically to unlock infrastructure land under litigation pressure is exactly the kind of move that can also touch forest, endowment or buffer-zone land near a Hyderabad JD site someday.
entries.src: Sources: Business Standard, The Federal & ANI (Tejasvi Surya reaction) · Cabinet clearance 21 Aug 2026; Surya's reaction published in the early hours of 23 Aug 2026 (exact clock time not otherwise stated)

entries.t: Amid resignation demands, Karnataka hands Minister Nagendra an ADDITIONAL charge — the Kalyana Karnataka development secretariat
entries.s: While BJP and JD(S) continue demanding B. Nagendra's resignation over the Valmiki Corporation scam, the Shivakumar-led government gave him an additional charge on top of his Planning & Statistics portfolio: the Kalyana Karnataka Region Development Secretariat, which administers the Article 371J special-development fund for the state's northeastern region. BJP called it politically provocative timing. Why it matters to you: a government doubling down on an accused minister, rather than removing him, is the clearest possible signal of where real power actually sits — a pattern to recognise anywhere a minister controls large discretionary development funds.
entries.src: Sources: Asianet Suvarna News, TV9 Kannada & Public TV Kannada · published 22 Aug 2026 (exact clock time not stated in source)

entries.t: Hyderabad's highest-ever government land sale: a Raidurg plot fetches ₹264 crore an acre
entries.s: TGIIC e-auctioned Plot P1, a 5.25-acre parcel in Raidurg, via the MSTC e-auction platform with JLL as transaction advisor. Against a ₹175-crore/acre reserve, bidding closed at ₹264 crore/acre — a 50.9% premium — for a total of ₹1,386 crore, won by MSN Realty. It beats TGIIC's own May 2026 Raidurg sale (₹237 crore/acre) by about 11%, and tops the previous city benchmark from HMDA's Kokapet/Neopolis auctions (~₹151 crore/acre). Why it matters to you: a clean, competitively-bid government auction price is the hardest number to argue with — ₹264 crore/acre is now the reference figure for IT-corridor land anywhere near Raidurg, useful leverage (or a reality check) the next time a JD partner quotes you a per-acre number in a comparable belt.
entries.src: Sources: Siasat , The Hans India & Deccan Chronicle · published 21 Aug 2026, 8:12 PM IST

entries.t: TG-RERA orders ₹42.2-lakh refund to Hyderabad plot buyers after the seller's cheques bounced
entries.s: TG-RERA ordered Trishakti Homes Consultancy to refund ₹42.2 lakh plus 10.7% interest (running from 7 June 2022) to buyers who had booked two plots in "Sree Rugveda Brundavanam Hills" in 2022, later cancelled, and were part-refunded before the rest bounced. The order finds the firm — a registered agent, not the builder — liable under Section 10 of the RERA Act for marketing an unregistered project. Why it matters to you: RERA can hold the selling agent personally liable, not just the builder — always verify a project's own RERA registration number before booking or accepting it into a JD.
entries.src: Source: Siasat · published 21 Aug 2026, 1:00 PM IST

entries.t: Section 22A fallout, day 4: employee unions reject the blame, helpline logs 400 complaints in 3 days
entries.s: Revenue department employee associations publicly pushed back on ministers pinning the prohibited-list crisis on "officials," calling it a policy failure. The state's toll-free 22A helpline logged 400 calls in its first three days — 116 on 20 August alone — with Rangareddy (23), Medchal-Malkajgiri (17), and Sangareddy & Siddipet (10 each) the top-complaint districts. Why it matters to you: the district breakdown is real diligence data — Rangareddy and Medchal-Malkajgiri are exactly the fast-growing plotting belts, so treat land there as higher 22A-risk until you've personally checked the live list.
entries.src: Sources: Telangana Today & Siasat · published 21 Aug 2026 (exact clock time not stated in source)

entries.t: Centre denies political clearance for Revanth's US leg; CM sends the Telangana Rising delegation on anyway
entries.s: After CM Revanth Reddy's delegation reached London on his 10-day UK-US "Telangana Rising" investment tour, the Ministry of External Affairs cleared only the UK leg — the US leg was denied. MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said the proposed US programme "was not appropriate to the office held." Revanth called the decision political, said he'd return to Hyderabad from London around 23 August, but directed the official delegation to proceed to the US anyway to sign MoUs with Harvard, MIT, Northeastern and Virginia Tech. Telangana BJP chief N. Ramchander Rao denied any "conspiracy." Why it matters to you: Centre-state friction can slow or reshape a state's investment pitch overnight — a reminder to price land on approvals actually cleared, not on a state government's travel-brochure ambitions.
entries.src: Sources: ANI (11:42 AM IST) & ANI (MEA statement) · published 21 Aug 2026, 5:43 PM IST

entries.t: Congress revolt: 20+ MLAs demand Konda Surekha's dismissal after she refuses to disown her daughter's attack on the CM
entries.s: After Minister Konda Surekha's written reply to the TPCC Disciplinary Committee called it a breach of "natural justice" to hold her responsible for daughter Konda Sushmita's attack on CM Revanth Reddy, over 20 Congress MLAs — led by Chief Whip Beerla Ilaiah and MLA Vemula Veeresham — held a press conference demanding her sacking from Cabinet and suspension from the party. AICC in-charge Meenakshi Natarajan sought a formal report; TPCC Disciplinary Committee chief Mallu Ravi warned that crossing the party's "Lakshman Rekha" invites action. Why it matters to you: the fastest-moving thread in the ₹200-crore-vs-₹7-crore Raviryal land-allotment story to watch — an internal Congress revolt could push this land-allotment allegation against the CM's brother into a far bigger story.
entries.src: Sources: Deccan Chronicle, The Hans India & ANI · published 21 Aug 2026 (exact clock time not stated in source)

entries.t: Polytechnic students' GO 97 protest reaches Nalgonda; BRS turns it into a Rahul Gandhi jab
entries.s: Protesting polytechnic students stopped Minister Komatireddy Venkat Reddy's convoy in Nalgonda over GO 97, which would fold polytechnic colleges into a new Young India Skill University; students say it would render their diplomas "useless." Separately, BRS's KTR and K. Kavitha invoked a 19 August Mahabubabad incident — a police inspector filmed grabbing a protesting student by the throat — to ask why Rahul Gandhi stays silent on "Congress police brutality" in Telangana. Why it matters to you: a reminder that a single state Government Order can restructure an entire institutional category overnight — the same sweeping-order power that created the Section 22A mess.
entries.src: Sources: Siasat, Telangana Today & ANI · published 21–22 Aug 2026 (KTR/Kavitha remarks: 22 Aug, 3:46 AM IST)

entries.t: CAG flags Telangana's ₹19,267-crore revenue deficit in the year's first four months
entries.s: CAG's report for April–July FY2026-27 showed Telangana's revenue deficit at ₹19,266.83 crore, with the fiscal deficit already at 57.7% of the full-year target (₹33,729.98 crore against a ₹58,458.71-crore estimate). BRS's KTR called the government "incompetent" on the finding. Why it matters to you: a state already 57.7% through its annual borrowing room in a third of the year has less headroom to fund the roads and ring roads that move land prices.
entries.src: Sources: Telangana Today, Daily Pioneer & The South First · published 21 Aug 2026 (exact clock time not stated in source)

entries.t: Karnataka Assembly passes a new Apartment Ownership law — and lets civic bodies seize neglected private roads for free
entries.s: Passed without discussion amid Assembly disruption, the Karnataka Apartment (Ownership and Management) Bill, 2026 replaces two 50-year-old laws for projects over 8 units: it mandates one registered RWA per project, sets a 75%-owner-consent threshold for redevelopment (dissenters bought out at 2x market value), requires 5-yearly structural safety audits for buildings over 30 years old, and obliges builders to fund maintenance on unsold flats. Two companion municipal bills let commissioners take over a dilapidated private layout road judged a safety risk and declare it public — with no compensation to its owner. Why it matters to you: any Bengaluru apartment redevelopment or JD now runs on a concrete 75%-consent-plus-2x-buyout formula — and a private access road inside a layout you thought was an asset can now be taken for free.
entries.src: Sources: Deccan Chronicle, Asianet Newsable, Construction World & Siasat · published 21 Aug 2026 (exact clock time not stated in source)

entries.t: Karnataka Assembly disrupted for a 5th day; BJP MLAs force their way in, Congress blocks its own Kharge resolution in retaliation
entries.s: BJP MLAs in black T-shirts, led by state chief B.Y. Vijayendra and LoP R. Ashoka, marched from the Valmiki statue to Vidhana Soudha demanding Minister B. Nagendra's resignation over the 2024 Valmiki ST welfare corporation scam, forcing past a security cordon; JD(S) joined. Nagendra refused to resign, calling it caste-based targeting, and said he'd answer on the Assembly floor. CM Shivakumar challenged the Opposition to file a formal debate notice. When Minister Muniyappa separately moved a resolution condemning a ritual after Congress chief Kharge's Haldwani rally, Ashoka withheld support unless Nagendra was sacked first — so it was dropped. The Assembly still passed 3 bills (including the Apartment Ownership Bill above) without discussion. Why it matters to you: a case study in how ministers accused of financial impropriety over discretionary government money get protected by coalition-math — recognise the same playbook wherever a state institution controls large discretionary funds or land allotments.
entries.src: Sources: Deccan Chronicle, ANI (10:36 AM IST), Deccan Herald & The News Minute · published 21 Aug 2026

entries.t: Frozen out of their own homes: hundreds converge on Telangana Bhavan as BRS opens a free legal cell for Section 22A victims
entries.s: Hundreds of Hyderabad-area owners whose land got wrongly frozen under the Section 22A “prohibited list” gathered at BRS headquarters seeking help. One case cited: Rajesh, HMT Housing Colony — bought his house on a bank loan in 2017, tried to sell it in 2026 after losing his job, and only discovered at registration that his survey number had been listed, despite the layout being HMDA-approved back in 1995. BRS announced a 10-lawyer free legal cell, led by advocate Kalyan, based at Telangana Bhavan. Why it matters to you: a plot can carry a clean sale deed, an approved layout, and 20+ years of tax receipts — and still freeze overnight if its survey number gets swept into 22A by a records-migration error. Check the live list before signing any JD, not just at diligence.
entries.src: Source: Telangana Today · published 19 Aug 2026 (exact clock time not stated in source)

entries.t: Hyderabad’s outer bypass stalls again: NHAI pushes Regional Ring Road North bid deadline to today — a sixth delay
entries.s: NHAI has extended the construction-bid deadline for the ₹8,500+ crore, 161-km Sangareddy–Choutuppal stretch (NH161AA, the RRR’s northern half) for the sixth time since the tender first opened in November 2025 — this time to today. Reported causes: pending Central alignment approvals, and the state pushing for the northern and southern packages to be executed together. Why it matters to you: land near a confirmed ring-road alignment re-rates sharply once acquisition and construction actually lock in — but every extension pushes that trigger further out, which matters for holding-period math on any land bank along the corridor.
entries.src: Source: Telangana Today · published today, 20 Aug 2026

entries.t: Harish Rao writes to Rahul Gandhi demanding the Revenue Minister’s removal; Ponguleti hits back: “like a murderer expressing condolences”
entries.s: BRS deputy floor leader T. Harish Rao’s open letter to LoP Rahul Gandhi demands Revenue Minister Ponguleti Srinivas Reddy’s dismissal, a judicial probe by a retired High Court judge, and a forensic audit of every 22A addition/removal since December 2023 — alleging a “30% commission” racket to get names off the list. Ponguleti hit back that BRS has “failed as the Opposition” and is “spreading falsehoods,” pointing to Dharani-era record flaws from the BRS government’s own tenure. Why it matters to you: if the forensic-audit demand ever succeeds, every 22A addition and removal since December 2023 becomes public record — the single best outcome for anyone buying land in the affected districts.
entries.src: Sources: Siasat and Siasat (Ponguleti’s reply) · published today, 20 Aug 2026 (exact clock time not stated in source)

entries.t: Minister’s daughter accuses CM Revanth of a ₹200-crore land favour to his brother; Congress serves a showcause notice on her mother
entries.s: After CM Revanth Reddy publicly endorsed the sitting Parkal MLA for renomination — blindsiding Minister Konda Surekha’s camp, which had been positioning daughter Konda Sushmita for the ticket — Sushmita called the government a “TDP Congress,” called the CM “arrogant,” and revived a land-allotment allegation: 5 acres at Raviryal handed to a company for ₹7 crore against an estimated ₹200-crore market value, benefiting the CM’s brother. Congress’s disciplinary committee gave Surekha 3 days to explain her daughter’s remarks; she submitted her reply the same evening. Why it matters to you: a ₹200-crore-vs-₹7-crore government land allotment involving the sitting CM’s own family is a live case study in the gap between allotment price and market price on discretionary government land — the exact gap worth checking before touching any government-linked parcel.
entries.src: Sources: The South First and ANI · published today, 20 Aug 2026

entries.t: CM Revanth calls delimitation “anti-South India” at Congress’s top body, then leaves for a 10-day UK–US investment tour
entries.s: At Wednesday’s CWC meeting in Delhi, Revanth warned that a uniform 50% Lok Sabha seat increase would let bigger, faster-growing northern states decide who forms the central government, and pushed weighting seats by economic contribution instead. He then left today for Oxford, Cambridge and London Business School, then Boston, through 30 August, pitching Telangana for education and investment tie-ups — sending Deputy CM Bhatti Vikramarka to represent the state at the Southern Zonal Council instead (full story in Karnataka Politics below).
entries.src: Sources: Siasat and Newsmeter · published today, 20 Aug 2026

entries.t: PSU telecom firm ITI puts 44 acres of prime K.R. Puram land up for e-auction at a ₹1,685-crore reserve price
entries.s: The National Land Monetization Corporation has invited e-auction bids for ITI Limited’s 44.03-acre, commercially-zoned, vacant parcel on Old Madras Road/NH-75 in Krishnarajapuram — a ₹38.28-crore-per-acre reserve, about 12% below ITI’s own July sale of a nearby 21-acre piece at ₹43.5 crore/acre. It’s one piece of a ₹13,500-crore national drive to monetise BSNL/MTNL/RINL-linked land; technical bids and EMD are due 16 September. Why it matters to you: a concrete, dated benchmark — ₹38–43 crore/acre for vacant, commercially-zoned, highway-facing land in an established IT corridor — worth keeping in your back pocket when discussing land-value trajectories with JD partners along Hyderabad’s own IT-corridor belts.
entries.src: Source: Business Standard · published 19 Aug 2026 (exact clock time not stated; reported same trading session)

entries.t: Karnataka’s Assembly stuck for a fourth straight day as the Opposition demands a minister’s resignation over a welfare-fund scam
entries.s: BJP and JD(S) disrupted the Karnataka Assembly for a fourth consecutive day, demanding Planning Minister B. Nagendra’s removal over 2024 embezzlement allegations at the Valmiki ST welfare corporation — he was reinducted into the cabinet on 3 August. LoP R. Ashoka displayed what he called a CBI chargesheet and claimed 24 pending cases; the Speaker adjourned the House for an hour. Nagendra calls it caste-based targeting and counters that 126 BJP ministers nationally carry criminal cases.
entries.src: Sources: IANS/Social News XYZ and ANI · published today, 20 Aug 2026 (Nagendra’s rebuttal: 19 Aug, 11:29 AM IST)

entries.t: Shivakumar tells the Centre: give the South its fair share of funds — and back Bengaluru’s Mekedatu water project
entries.s: At the 31st Southern Zonal Council, Karnataka CM D.K. Shivakumar told Union Home Minister Amit Shah that Karnataka’s Finance Commission tax share fell from 4.7% to 3.6% — a claimed ₹65,000-crore loss over six years — despite the state holding 5.5% of India’s population but generating ~9% of GDP and 42% of software exports. He defended the long-stalled Mekedatu dam as securing Bengaluru’s drinking water, raised the Upper Bhadra irrigation project, and asked the Centre to reconsider the new Mines and Minerals Act. Why it matters to you: Mekedatu’s fate is a leading indicator for Bengaluru’s long-term water security — the same “where’s the water coming from” question worth asking of any long-horizon Hyderabad land bet.
entries.src: Source: ANI · published today, 20 Aug 2026, 12:56 PM IST (Southern Zonal Council, Kovalam, chaired by Amit Shah at 10:55 AM IST)
